items.b: 8,881 English Wikipedia articles are about Uganda, drawing 428.9 million views since July 2015. 1,728 of them (19%) have been read fewer than 1,000 times in all.

“Zohran Mamdani” alone accounts for 6.6% of all views. The ten most read articles hold 24% and the top hundred 54%. Many of the biggest draws are people with a Ugandan link who are famous worldwide, so views say little about how much Uganda itself is being read.
27% of articles are stubs and 6,006 (68%) sit at Start class; only 298 (3.4%) reach B or better. Classes are estimated from length for most articles, so read them as depth, not polish.
An article rated B or better draws 496,562 views on average, against 5,403 for a stub — about 92 times more.
1,268 articles are read a great deal yet remain stubs or Start class. Together they hold 94.8 million views (22% of the total). Improving them is the highest-return work in the whole project.
45% of the articles (4,032) have a Luganda counterpart; 4,849 do not. English-language readers of Ugandan topics are mostly not offered a Luganda page.
67% of articles (5,909) have no lead image — the quickest improvement is often a photo from Commons, where Uganda now has more than 60,000 files.
3,777 articles are about people. Of those with a recorded gender, 36% are women (1,339) and 2,430 are men. Among 100 notable people with no English article, 34 are women.
The most productive year was 2014, with 579 articles created. Views peaked in 2025, at 66 million.
Central holds 64% of regional articles; the least covered region is Northern with 14%.
Only 2% of rural places on Wikidata have an English article, against 8% of urban ones.
Beyond the existing articles: 100 notable people and 150 items with articles in other languages still have no English article, and 104 articles sit in no category.
The self-declared community list holds 316 editors, of whom 172 were active in the last year and 100 accounts are new this year.

blocks.title: Women and men with an article, compared
rows: Shares are of each group: "Women stubs" is the share of women's articles that are stubs. A person with no recorded binary gender is left out of the comparison. Categories with fewer than thirty such people are omitted. Women are less often stubs and far more often in Luganda than men; they are the minority of biographies and are read less.

blocks.title: Living and deceased, by gender
rows: Living means no death date and born in 1906 or later. Many Ugandan biographies carry neither date on Wikidata, which is itself a gap.

blocks.text: This counts editors located in Uganda, not editors of Ugandan content. Nothing public ties an editor's country to the articles they touched. From mid-2023 the figures carry deliberate noise of a few editors either way.

insights.b: 8,881 English Wikipedia articles are about Uganda, drawing 428.9 million views since July 2015. 1,728 of them (19%) have been read fewer than 1,000 times in all.

“Zohran Mamdani” alone accounts for 6.6% of all views. The ten most read articles hold 24% and the top hundred 54%. Many of the biggest draws are people with a Ugandan link who are famous worldwide, so views say little about how much Uganda itself is being read.
27% of articles are stubs and 6,006 (68%) sit at Start class; only 298 (3.4%) reach B or better. Classes are estimated from length for most articles, so read them as depth, not polish.
An article rated B or better draws 496,562 views on average, against 5,403 for a stub — about 92 times more.
1,268 articles are read a great deal yet remain stubs or Start class. Together they hold 94.8 million views (22% of the total). Improving them is the highest-return work in the whole project.
45% of the articles (4,032) have a Luganda counterpart; 4,849 do not. English-language readers of Ugandan topics are mostly not offered a Luganda page.
67% of articles (5,909) have no lead image — the quickest improvement is often a photo from Commons, where Uganda now has more than 60,000 files.
3,777 articles are about people. Of those with a recorded gender, 36% are women (1,339) and 2,430 are men. Among 100 notable people with no English article, 34 are women.
The most productive year was 2014, with 579 articles created. Views peaked in 2025, at 66 million.
Central holds 64% of regional articles; the least covered region is Northern with 14%.
Only 2% of rural places on Wikidata have an English article, against 8% of urban ones.
Beyond the existing articles: 100 notable people and 150 items with articles in other languages still have no English article, and 104 articles sit in no category.
The self-declared community list holds 316 editors, of whom 172 were active in the last year and 100 accounts are new this year.
